slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: I feel sick. Body parts. Getting help." Mime "I feel sick."
Before class: print the Student Pages (number expected + 3 spares), one set of picture cards per group of 3–4, body-part picture cards, the emergency card and medicine label, mini whiteboards or scrap paper. Have the phone + small speaker and L1_L12_listening.mp3 ready. Prep time: 30 min.
Practice only. Never ask learners to share real medical details. If a learner starts a real medical story, stop gently and return to the picture. The 911 dialogue is not a real emergency.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Real-World Reading, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson12/Level1_Lesson12.md (At a glance, Clock-time plan, How to Use This Plan).

runs.t: I can say: I feel sick. / I'm hurt.
I can ask: Are you OK? Where does it hurt?
I can say: Call 911. Sit down.
I can read a medicine label and a card.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: name basic body parts.
Goal 2: say "How do you feel? I feel sick. / I'm hurt."
Goal 3: ask "Are you OK? What's wrong? Where does it hurt?"
Goal 4: use help commands: "Call 911. Sit down. Go to the doctor."
Goal 5: read a simple medicine label and emergency card (7:15).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson12/Level1_Lesson12.md (At a glance: Objectives).

runs.t: B: It's next to the bank.

slides.notes:
Pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: Where's the pharmacy? How do you feel? Are you OK?
Model with one learner: "Where's the pharmacy?" → "It's next to the bank." Then "How do you feel?" → "I feel sick."
Click to show the A question. Click again for the answers. Pairs use the Hello + Review page: 1 Where's the pharmacy? → It's ___. 2 Turn left or turn right? 3 Where's the pharmacy? → It's ___. Switch. Then find a new partner.
Homework check (last 3 min): partners show last week's homework. Walk around and look.
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. If behind: one partner only.

slides.notes:
Point to the body pictures: "Head. Stomach. Arm. Leg." Point to your own head, eye, ear, mouth, arm, hand.
Click to show each picture. Point and say the word. Learners repeat 2 times. ★ words 2 more times.
★ = most important words (as on the New Words page). eye, ear, and mouth have no ★. If behind: teach the ★ words only.

runs.t: Part 1: Rosa and Marco at work.

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Part one: Rosa and Marco are at work. Part two: practice only — a call to 9 1 1. Not a real emergency."
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (how Marco feels; where it hurts). Listen 2: Task B (write the address number). Listen 3: Task C (check what Rosa says).
Say it!: class repeats: "I feel sick." "Where does it hurt?" "It hurts here."
The audio L1_L12_listening.mp3 (about 1:10) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say "practice only" before you play part two.
Voices: Narrator, Rosa, Marco, Operator, Ana. Synthetic voices made with Chatterbox TTS (MIT), copied from short reference clips made with Kokoro-82M (Apache 2.0); no recordings of real people.
If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

slides.title: Before You Listen

slides.notes:
Listen 1 (Task A). Learners circle: 1 Marco feels sick or tired; 2 it hurts: head, stomach, or arm.
Listen 2 (Task B, part two, practice only): learners write the address number.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer: 1 sick, 2 stomach, 3 210 (210 Pine Street).
In the audio: "No, I'm not. I feel sick." "It hurts here. My stomach." "Two ten Pine Street."
The address is invented (210 Pine Street). Part two is practice only — not a real emergency.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson12/Level1_Lesson12.md (Step 3: Listening; Student Pages: Listening A and B; Answer key; Teacher notes).
slides.title: Listening A + B

slides.notes:
Listen 3 (Task C): learners check what Rosa says. Pairs compare. Then click to show the answer.
Task C: Sit down ✓, Go home ✓, Call the doctor ✓ ("Sit down. Do you need water?" "OK. Go home. Call the doctor."). Rosa does not say "Call 911" (as in the answer key).
Part two of the audio (practice only): Ana says "It hurts here. My arm." The address is 210 Pine Street. The operator says "Help is coming."
Task D (practice only — not a real emergency): A asks "Are you OK?" "Where does it hurt?" Click to show B's answers: "No, I'm not. I feel sick." "Here. My stomach." Then switch.
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. Left = question. Right = answer. Point left, then right.
Box 1: "How do you feel?" Click: "I feel sick. / I feel tired." "Are you OK?" Click: "No, I'm not. I'm sick."
Box 2: "What's wrong?" Click: "I'm hurt." "Where does it hurt?" Click: "It hurts here." Point to a picture, not to a real problem.
Check question: "I ___ sick." (feel / am)
Level 1 says "It hurts here" + point. "My head hurts" is for Level 2.

Call 911 (not "Call to 911").
Check question: "Call ___" (911)

slides.notes:
Box 5: I need… + a doctor. / help. / water. Example: I need to go home.
"Do you need a doctor?" Click: "Yes. I need a doctor." (as in the audio).
Right box: "What do you need?" Click: "I need help. / I need water. / I need to go home."

slides.title: Grammar Box 5

slides.notes:
Read each left line. Click to show the right line. Learners repeat it.
Line 1: "I'm sick or I have sick?" Say "I'm sick. I'm tired. I'm cold." (not "I have sick").
Line 2: "Do we say My head hurts in Level 1?" Learners may hear it. In this lesson, say "It hurts here" and point. Level 2 practices "My ___ hurts".
Side card: "Do I say real medical problems in class?" No. Use the pictures. Point and say "Here."
Practice only. Never ask learners to share real medical details. If a learner starts a real medical story, stop gently and return to the picture.

runs.t: Write feel, hurts, OK, or Call.

slides.notes:
Learners write feel, hurts, OK, or Call. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 feel, 2 OK, 3 hurts, 4 Call, 5 feel.
Line 6 on the page: learners write one sentence (answers will vary).

slides.title: Practice

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
I have sick → I'm sick. I have hungry → I'm hungry. Call to 911 → Call 911.
Spanish speakers: I'm sick / I'm tired / I'm cold (no "I have…"). My head hurts = Me duele la cabeza (Level 2 practices it). Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
Tip for speakers of other languages: read the grammar boxes left to right. Copy one question and one answer.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson12/Level1_Lesson12.md (Grammar: Common mistakes).

slides.notes:
Part 2 (5 min). Groups of 3: practice 911 role play from the emergency card. This is not a real call. Switch roles.

Then: "It hurts here. My ___." "What's the address?" Learners read the street from the card (practice address: 210 Pine St).
Remind: in a real emergency, call 911. Today is practice only.

slides.title: 911 Practice

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says "I feel sick." or "It hurts here." or "Call 911."
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1, line 1 together. Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) write the body part (head, arm, stomach, leg); 2) unscramble: feel / I / sick; you / Are / OK; hurts / It / here; 3) copy the emergency card: write your name and a phone number you choose to share (or invent); 4) ask a family member "How do you feel?" and write the answer; 5) review: write one direction (Lesson 11).

slides.title: In an Emergency

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each word slowly, 2 times: 1 sick, 2 head, 3 doctor, 4 arm, 5 stomach. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 b, 2 a, 3 c, 4 d.
Part C answers: 1 feel (I feel sick.), 2 hurts (It hurts here.), 3 Call (Call 911.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces. Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. Not a test grade. Collect if you want. If behind: do it next week at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson12/Level1_Lesson12.md (Progress Check step; Student Pages: Progress Check; Answer key).
